laterite-terracotta.usage: Mark, primary action, selected option, cap Seal, and the field of two full-bleed bands.

clay-tint.usage: Defined; not used by a component.

blush-tint.usage: Field of the can't-do band; hover fill of an unselected cap option.

chalk-surface.usage: Interface fragment cards; hover fill of the cream primary action.

char-course.usage: Defined; not used by a component.

display.purpose: Hero only. Archivo 900, uppercase, pitch 0.886em, widths mixed per course (114 / 110 / 125; 110 at 720px and below). Never wraps.

headline.purpose: One per band, four words at most, sentence case with a full stop. Archivo 900 at width 125, balanced, may wrap to two lines. Can't-do band clamp(2.6rem, 5.4vw, 6.4rem); closing band clamp(3rem, 7.2vw, 8.6rem).

title.purpose: The hero's single supporting sentence. Archivo 700 at width 108, balanced, max 23em. Drops to clamp(1rem, 1.42vw, 1.75rem) in the wide-and-short layout.

action.purpose: Button labels, sentence case, Archivo 700 at width 105. Closing action clamp(1.125rem, 2.6vw, 2.6rem); nav Launch clamp(14px, 1.3vw, 25px).

body.purpose: Inherited default: Archivo 400 at width 100. The only running Archivo below the hero is the can't-do list: weight 500, width 102, clamp(1.0625rem, 1.62vw, 1.85rem).

figure.purpose: The wall's running total. Card figures use the same voice at tracking 0: cap figure clamp(1.9rem, 4.9vw, 5.4rem), wallet row clamp(1.8rem, 4.5vw, 5rem).

receipt.purpose: The one sentence a band is allowed, in mono sentence case, twelve words at most; also the footer legal line at clamp(11px, 1.15vw, 18px). The cap sentence is set tight, clamp(13px, 1.4vw, 23px), on one line above 720px.

label.purpose: Chips, next cue, nav link, dates, card labels, notes. Uppercase, tabular, tracking 0.14em (global .mono) opening to 0.16-0.18em inside bands. Tickers keep their case.

shadows.name: kiln-edge
shadows.purpose: Solid bottom edge of the terracotta primary action: thickness, not light. Paired with an equal margin-bottom.

shadows.name: kiln-edge-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover: the button sinks 35% of its edge.

shadows.name: soot-edge
shadows.purpose: The same edge under the cream primary action on a terracotta band; same hover (65%) and press (0).

shadows.name: brick-contact
shadows.purpose: The only soft shadows in the system. Part of the rasters; never recreated in CSS.

motion.name: ease-lay
motion.purpose: The only easing. Drop and settle, no bounce.

motion.name: dur-lay
motion.purpose: Base duration for all state transitions (hover, press, underline, arrow, option select).

motion.name: lay
motion.purpose: Display courses drop into place, top course first.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: 980ms ease-lay 320ms both; 0% opacity 0 translateY(-0.95em) rotate(-10deg); 12% opacity 1; 62% translateY(0.012em) rotate(0.6deg); 100% none
motion.purpose: The brick drops, presses slightly past rest and settles. Replayed on click.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: 420ms ease-lay both; clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 -4% 0 0); delays 750 / 900 / 1050ms
motion.purpose: Flow labels wipe in from the left.

motion.name: draw
motion.value: 380ms ease-lay both; stroke-dasharray 60, stroke-dashoffset 60 to 0; delays 850 / 1000 / 1150ms
motion.purpose: Leader lines draw toward the brick. Sequence ends at about 1530ms.

motion.name: pointer-drift
motion.value: translate calc(var(--px) * 10px) calc(var(--py) * 8px); rotate calc(var(--px) * 1.2deg); transition 600ms ease-lay; --px and --py in [-0.5, 0.5]; mouse pointers only
motion.purpose: The brick follows the pointer by a few pixels.

motion.name: band-entrance
motion.value: transition: transform 620ms ease-lay; [data-in=true] none, otherwise translateY(-14px); useInView threshold 0.35 reports true until hydration, then fires once
motion.purpose: The only entrance below the hero: copy and visual drop and settle. Server-rendered settled; transform only, never opacity.

motion.name: payday-drop
motion.value: transition: transform 640ms ease-lay; from translateY(-46px); transition-delay index * 110ms; useInView threshold 0.5
motion.purpose: Laid payday bricks drop onto the baseline one after another. Server-rendered on the baseline.

motion.name: payday-fall
motion.value: transform: translateY(calc((1 - var(--fall)) * -56%)) rotate(calc((1 - var(--fall)) * 14deg)); --fall = slice(progress, 0.34, 0.66)
motion.purpose: Today's brick falls as the band scrolls by. Reduced motion: held at translateY(-30%) rotate(9deg).

motion.name: wall-lay
motion.value: laid = round(slice(progress, 0.16, 0.56) * 52); unlaid brick opacity 0, translateY(-34px); transition transform 520ms ease-lay, opacity 160ms linear
motion.purpose: The wall fills from the bottom course up as the band scrolls; the figure is 25 x laid. Server-rendered full; bricks are lifted only after hydration.

motion.name: spine-lay
motion.value: laid = floor((innerHeight * 0.74 - spine.top) / spine.height * 52); unlaid face opacity 0, translateY(-10px); transition transform 420ms ease-lay, opacity 140ms linear
motion.purpose: The spine gains a brick for every stretch the visitor has read. Server-rendered full.

motion.name: stamp
motion.value: animation: 420ms ease-lay backwards; from transform: scale(1.24) rotate(-7deg)
motion.purpose: A seal comes down hard and stays put. Always rendered; scale plus rotate, transform only. Replays on every cap change (wrapper re-keyed).

motion.name: wallet-count
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame, 1100ms, ease-out cubic, 0.4532 to 0.4944; initial state is the final value
motion.purpose: The wallet grows by one brick when its band enters. Screen readers get the final value only.

motion.name: slice
motion.purpose: Remaps a window of a band's scroll progress onto 0..1 with an ease-out. useScrollProgress measures at most once per frame and returns 1 at once under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): hero lay/settle/reveal/draw animation none; drift none; .lays, .dropped, wall bricks transform none and transition none; unlaid wall bricks opacity 1; spine transition none and fully laid; stamp animation none; falling brick held at translateY(-30%) rotate(9deg); wallet count skipped; globally *, *::before, *::after { transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important }
motion.purpose: Every motion has a still alternative, including hover and press.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Four-course hero; bands collapse to one column; spine hidden; five-per-course wall; four paydays; footer stacks.

brandAssets.status: Shipped in packages/ui/brand/. The symbol and wordmark are used by the nav and footer. The five state seals and the running-bond tiles are not used by the page: the Seal is drawn in code and the wall is built from a brick raster. They remain available assets.

rasters.status: placeholder; to be replaced by a commissioned render at the same framing
placeholder; to be replaced by a commissioned render at the same framing

components.name: Seal
components.description: A brickmaker's stamp drawn in code so it takes live values. Two borders, a main line in Archivo 900 (width 112) or, for longer stamps, Martian Mono 600 in a wider viewBox. Colour is currentColor: terracotta on a card, lime on a terracotta band. An feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap filter roughens the ink; its seed is derived from the stamp text (character codes summed, mod 97), so no two stamps share the same roughness. Always rendered; only the press is animated (scale and twist, no opacity). Decorative when the words are already on the page, otherwise role=img with a label.

components.name: Payday strip
components.description: One brick every payday, on a terracotta band. A 3px lime baseline with a tick per payday is painted under the bricks; mono dates hang below. Three states: dropped (laid bricks fall 46px into place, staggered 110ms), falling (today's brick, tied to scroll progress; the snippet holds it at 40% of its fall, and reduced motion holds it at translateY(-30%) rotate(9deg)), ahead (dashed lime outline). The raster is a placeholder.
components.html:
1. Sep 05
  2. Sep 12
  3. Sep 19
  4. Sep 26
  5. Oct 03
components.css: .ds-strip-field { padding: clamp(64px, 9vw, 150px) var(--gutter) clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 76px); background: var(--laterite); color: var(--lime); overflow: clip; } .ds-strip { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); margin: 0; padding: 0 0 clamp(34px, 3vw, 52px); list-style: none; } .ds-strip::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: calc(clamp(34px, 3vw, 52px) - 3px); height: 3px; background: var(--lime); } .ds-payday { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } .ds-payday::after { content: ""; position: absolute; bottom: -12px; width: 3px; height: 12px; background: var(--lime); z-index: 1; } .ds-date { position: absolute; bottom: calc(-1 * clamp(34px, 3vw, 52px)); font-family: var(--font-martian-mono), 'Martian Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: clamp(10px, 1vw, 16px); letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-strip-brick { position: relative; z-index: 1; display: block; width: 92%; height: auto; user-select: none; } .ds-dropped { animation: ds-drop 640ms var(--ease-lay) backwards; } .ds-payday:nth-child(2) .ds-dropped { animation-delay: 110ms; } .ds-payday:nth-child(3) .ds-dropped { animation-delay: 220ms; } @keyframes ds-drop { from { transform: translateY(-46px); } } .ds-falling { --fall: 0.4; transform: translateY(calc((1 - var(--fall)) * -56%)) rotate(calc((1 - var(--fall)) * 14deg)); } .ds-ahead { position: relative; z-index: 1; width: 86%; aspect-ratio: 2.15 / 1; margin-bottom: 6px; border: 2px dashed var(--lime); border-radius: 6px; opacity: 0.85; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-dropped { animation: none; } .ds-falling { transform: translateY(-30%) rotate(9deg); } }

components.name: The wall (running bond) and figure
components.description: 52 bricks in running bond on soot: seven per course wide, five narrow (both rendered, CSS picks one), numbered from the bottom course up. Offset courses shift half a brick and carry a clipped half-brick. 1.5px slot padding (3px between neighbours), 2px radius, four turns so repeats do not read as a pattern; open slots in the top course are dashed. The mono figure is 25 x bricks laid, captioned 'Laid, not promised'. Server-rendered full; bricks lift away only after hydration and land as the band scrolls. The snippet shows the top four courses at a fixed brick width; the build uses (100vw - spine) / cols. The raster is a 640px placeholder used as a CSS background.
components.html: $1,300.00Laid, not promised

narrative.overview:
Laterite is red earth cut into bricks that harden with time. The system treats the screen as a printer's forme: heavy type is locked up in courses like brick, the gaps between courses are mortar joints, and one real brick sits in the hero where a word would go. Everything else is annotation in a monospaced hand: amounts, dates, labels, receipt lines, outlined chips, stamped seals. The stance is anti-hype: slow, solid, in plain sight.

The page is one scroll: a soot nav band, the type-wall hero, seven full-bleed bands of flat colour with a 52-brick spine running down their right edge, and a one-row soot footer. Each band holds one idea and one large visual: an interface fragment, a strip of bricks, a wall. This record describes what ships. Tokens live in `packages/ui/src/styles.css`; hero geometry in `components/hero.module.css`; the bands in `components/story/story.module.css`.

Fields are flat and warm. There are no gradients, glows, blurs or drop shadows anywhere in the build. The only photographic material is the brick. The direction contract embedded in `app/layout.tsx` says the same: colours are whole fields or objects, the brick is the only photographic material, seals are drawn in code.
keyCharacteristics: Type is the structure. The hero headline is a wall measured in em of its course size; band headlines run at 7.5vw.
Four field colours (lime, terracotta, soot, blush) in full-bleed bands; no two adjacent bands share a field.
Two voices: Archivo for words, Martian Mono for every amount, date, label, chip, receipt line and card.
Everything derives from the brick: running bond, tight joints, small radii, brick-end spine.
One motion grammar, "lay a brick": drop and settle, no bounce. Scroll lays the bricks.
Finished by default: the server renders the full wall, the final figure and every seal; nothing is hidden on first paint.
Depth comes from thickness, never from light: a solid edge under the primary action, a contact shadow baked into the brick rasters.

rules.name: The Object Or Field Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is either a whole object or a whole field, never words. As an object on a light field it is the mark, the primary action (and a selected option), the brick and its stamp. As a field it is a full-bleed band, at most two per page and never adjacent; on it everything is lime and the primary action inverts to cream with a soot edge. It is never a heading color, a link color, a partial wash or a chart series.

rules.name: The Negation In Ink Rule
rules.body: "No", "can't" and "never" are drawn in soot, like the can't-do crosses. Red is the brand, never a warning.

rules.name: The Red Is Not Loss Rule
rules.body: Red is the brand. A loss is slate with a minus sign. Danger is cold crimson with an icon. A gain is moss. Color never carries the meaning alone; the sign, the icon or the word does.

rules.name: The Lime On Dark Rule
rules.body: On soot and on terracotta, all text is lime, including the footer's legal line. Terracotta on soot may be a shape (the symbol, 3.33:1), never words. Dark bands carry the `.on-dark` class so focus rings flip to lime.

rules.name: The Alternating Field Rule
rules.body: Band order is lime, terracotta, lime, soot, blush, lime, terracotta, then the soot footer. Lime is the rest between statements; no two neighbours share a field.

rules.name: The Justified Forme Rule
rules.body: The hero's display courses are justified by mixing widths, not by changing size or tracking. The first course sets the measure; later courses are set narrower or wider (110 to 125) to reach their mark. Each course carries its own negative left margin (-0.042em to -0.078em) so its first stem sits on the gutter.

rules.name: The Mortar Rule
rules.body: Hero course pitch is 0.886em. With Archivo's 0.686em cap height that leaves a 0.2em joint between courses. The joint is part of the design: annotation (the flow label row) is set inside it, and nothing else may close it.

rules.name: The Receipt Line Rule
rules.body: Support copy under a band headline is one sentence, twelve words at most, set in mono sentence case like a line on a receipt. Bands never carry Archivo paragraphs.

rules.name: The Ticker Rule
rules.body: Mono labels are uppercase except tickers, which keep their own case (`SPYx`, via `text-transform: none` in the hero flow row).

rules.name: The One Left Edge Rule
rules.body: Nav, hero type, bands and footer all take their horizontal inset from `--gutter` (the bands' `--pad-x` is `var(--gutter)`), so the logo, the hero's first stem, every band headline and the footer lockup share one left edge: 20px on phones, 41px at 1440, 55px at 1920 and up. Never give a section its own inset.

rules.name: The First Viewport Rule
rules.body: The primary action is inside the first viewport, in every hero layout. In the tall and wide layouts the course size yields to viewport height. On short phones the brick gives up size and the action moves ahead of the sentence. When space runs out, the sentence yields; the action never does.

rules.name: The One Idea Rule
rules.body: A band holds one headline, at most one receipt line, and one large visual. Nothing else: no kicker, no section number, no second paragraph, no card grid.

rules.name: The Thickness Rule
rules.body: A thing may have a bottom edge if it is a brick you can press. Only the primary action qualifies, in either colourway. The nav Launch button is flat and moves 2px on press. Cards are flat. Nothing floats.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Not Yet Rule
rules.body: A 2px dashed outline marks a brick that has not been laid: the payday still ahead (lime on terracotta), the open slots in the wall's top course (lime at 70%), the unread bricks of the spine (soot at 55%). Solid is laid. Dashes are never decoration.

rules.name: The Finished By Default Rule
rules.body: The server renders the finished page, in state and in position: the wall full, the figure at `$1,300.00`, the spine full, every seal stamped, the wallet at its final balance, band copy and payday bricks settled (`data-in="true"`). Things are lifted away only after hydration, when the script asks, and then laid again as the visitor reaches them. In the hero, resting CSS is the visible state and keyframes animate FROM hidden with `animation-fill-mode: both`. Nothing depends on JavaScript or an observer to become visible.

rules.name: The Transform Only Rule
rules.body: Below the hero, entrances move; they never fade. The band entrance, the payday drop and the stamp animate `transform` alone, so content is readable before, during and without the animation. Opacity is used only for bricks the script has already lifted out of a finished wall or spine (and, in the hero, for the first 12% of the brick's own settle).

rules.name: The Still Alternative Rule
rules.body: Every motion has a still alternative, including hover and press. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: hero animations and pointer drift are removed; band entrances, payday drops and stamps are off; the wall and spine render full and the figure final; the wallet shows its final value; the falling brick holds its tilted pose; and a global rule sets every transition to 0.01ms with `scroll-behavior: auto`, so hover and press change instantly.

dos: **Do** treat terracotta as an object or a whole field: the mark, the primary action, the brick and its stamp, or a full-bleed band. Hover is ember; the edge is kiln.
**Do** alternate band fields (lime, terracotta, lime, soot, blush, lime, terracotta) and set everything on soot or terracotta in lime.
**Do** give each band one headline (four words, Archivo 900 at width 125, 7.5vw), at most one mono receipt line (twelve words), and one large visual.
**Do** set every amount, date, address, label, chip, card and receipt line in Martian Mono with tabular figures. Labels are uppercase and tracked 0.14em or wider; keep ticker case (`SPYx`).
**Do** measure anything attached to the hero type in em of the course size, and justify its courses by mixing Archivo widths (110 to 125) at weight 900, pitch 0.886em.
**Do** show product UI as a flat fragment card: chalk, 2px soot border, 14px radius, mono, with native form controls underneath.
**Do** draw seals with the Seal component, feed them live values, and mark them `decorative` when the words are already on the page.
**Do** build repeated units as bricks: running bond, numbered bottom-up, 2 to 3px radius, 3px between neighbours, dashed when not yet laid.

**Do** render the finished state on the server, position included, and lift things away only after hydration. Drive scroll pieces with `useScrollProgress` and `slice`, entrances with `useInView` and `transform`.
**Do** ship a still alternative for every motion, hover and press included.
**Do** keep the primary action inside the first viewport, with an edge that compresses on press; on terracotta it is cream with a soot edge.
**Do** state the cap wherever the mechanism is shown, frame every illustrative amount as an example, and caption any total as laid, not promised.
**Do** render a link only when it has a real destination.
**Do** draw negation in soot: crosses, "can't", "never". Red is the brand, never a warning.
**Do** inset every section by `--gutter` so nav, hero, bands and footer share one left edge.
**Do** pair every semantic color with a sign, icon or word. Loss is slate with a minus sign; danger is cold crimson with an icon; gain is moss.
**Do** use the vocabulary: Brick (one purchase), Course (one period), Cap (permission limit), First course (trial week), Laid (executed), The wall (history).
**Do** replace the three placeholder rasters with commissioned renders at the same framing, and request any new produced imagery with exact specs.
donts: **Don't** use any photographic material other than the brick: no people, scenes, devices, coins or other objects. The hero keeps a single brick; below it the brick repeats only as masonry (strip, wall, spine).
**Don't** set terracotta as text, as a link color, or as a partial wash. Never terracotta words on soot (3.33:1), blush (3.87:1) or sand (3.94:1).
**Don't** use red for loss, error or decline. Red is the brand.
**Don't** use purple, neon lime, mint or bank blue. Lime here means the cream mortar color only.
**Don't** use gradients, glow, blur, drop shadows, or a CSS shadow on a brick. Flat fields only; depth is a solid bottom edge.
**Don't** show candlestick charts or a line chart of the index going up, and don't present a figure that could be read as a return.
**Don't** lay out a grid of identical cards, put a device frame around a fragment, or add kickers, eyebrows or section numbers to bands.
**Don't** fade content in on scroll, hide anything until an observer fires, or let hydration shift the layout (render both variants and let CSS pick, as the wall does with its two bonds).
**Don't** bounce, spring or overshoot upward. Things drop and settle.
**Don't** let a hero course wrap, close a mortar joint, or fake a weight or width (`font-synthesis: none`).
**Don't** put the hero brick, the wall, the spine or any replay flourish in the tab order or the accessibility tree.
**Don't** use icon fonts or glyph icons; arrows and crosses are drawn strokes.
**Don't** render placeholder links, invent traction (counts, logos, press, testimonials), or promise returns, yield or urgency.
**Don't** capitalize the wordmark or recolor the marks outside terracotta, cream and ink.
